name: Chadian Daraba
description: Daraba, a genuine Chadian everyday stew, real technique combines okra, eggplant, and sweet potato together with greens - not just okra alone - all simmered in a bouillon-seasoned broth before real peanut butter is whisked in. Real versions are boldly seasoned with black pepper and cayenne; one longtime cook describes it as 'fiery even without the chili', so don't be shy with the pepper here.

ingredients_full.note: tsp, generous - real daraba is boldly peppery

ingredients.note: tsp, generous - real daraba is boldly peppery

steps_detailed: Combine the eggplant, sweet potato, and tomatoes with 2 cups water, the bouillon, black pepper, and chili powder, being generous with both.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the okra and spinach, and simmer 8-10 minutes more.
Whisk the peanut butter with a little of the hot broth until smooth, then stir back into the pot and simmer 5 minutes more until thickened.

name: Chadian Boule (Millet Paste)
description: Boule, a stiff millet porridge, is Chad's most essential staple starch, closely related to tô and other Sahelian pastes - millet flour isn't a distinct item here, so cornmeal stands in for a similarly stiff texture.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring vigorously, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and it pulls away from the sides of the pot.

name: Chadian Peanut Squash Stew
description: A peanut and squash stew, real technique frying the squash with spices first before adding water, building real depth rather than just boiling everything together.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Fry the squash and onion in the oil with the cumin, being generous with the spice, 6-7 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water and simmer 20-22 minutes until the squash is tender.
Stir in the chopped peanuts just before serving for texture.

name: Chadian Mullah Tagalia
description: Mullah tagalia, a red stew thickened with real ground dried okra, shared with neighboring Sudan, real versions boldly seasoned rather than mild.

ingredients_full.note: sliced then ground into a fine powder

ingredients.note: sliced then ground into a fine powder

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then add the coriander and cinnamon, being generous with both.
Add the diced tomatoes and 1.5 cups water, and simmer 20 minutes.
Whisk the ground okra with a little cool water and stir in, simmering 5-8 minutes more until thickened.

name: Chadian Aiyash
description: Aiyash, millet dough balls dipped in savory sauces, is a common dish among Chadian Arab communities - real millet isn't a distinct item here, so cornmeal stands in.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick.
Shape into small balls for dipping into sauces.

name: Chadian Grilled Meat
description: Grilled meat generously seasoned with black pepper and garlic, a beloved Chadian dish for gatherings.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and pepper, being generous with both.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Chadian Ful Medames
description: Ful medames, slow-cooked fava beans, shared across the wider Sahel and North African region, real Chadian versions generous with cumin.
steps_detailed: Simmer the fava beans with a splash of water, 8-10 minutes, until very soft.
Mash roughly and stir in the garlic, lemon juice, cumin (be generous), and olive oil.

name: Chadian Millet Sweet Cookies (Ouaddai)
description: Ouaddai, sweet fried cookies made from millet flour, sugar, and egg, a beloved Chadian snack - real millet flour isn't a distinct item here, so all-purpose flour stands in.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, sugar, and egg into a firm dough.
Roll out and cut into small pieces.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes, until golden.

name: Chadian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Chadian home cooking, real versions boldly seasoned with black pepper.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, tomatoes, and pepper, being generous with the pepper, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Chadian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed generously with garlic and pepper, reflecting Chad's Lake Chad fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and pepper, being generous with both.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Chadian Bean Fritters
description: Fried black-eyed pea fritters, closely related to akara found across West and Central Africa.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Blend the cowpeas with the onion into a thick batter.
Whip briefly to add air, then fry spoonfuls, turning, 4-5 minutes, until golden.

description: Simple fried sweet potato, a common Chadian side dish, real versions generously seasoned with black pepper.
steps_detailed: Fry the sweet potato wedges, turning, 6-8 minutes, until golden and tender inside.
Season with pepper while still hot, being generous.

name: Chadian Coleslaw
description: A mayonnaise-dressed cabbage salad, a common Chadian side, real versions with a touch of mustard for depth.
steps_detailed: Whisk the mayonnaise and mustard together.
Toss with the cabbage and carrot until well coated.

name: Chadian Tomato Onion Salad
description: A simple tomato and onion salad, a common Chadian side, real technique letting the onion sit briefly in lemon juice first.
steps_detailed: Toss the onion with the lemon juice and let sit 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and toss together.

name: Chadian Peanut Sauce
description: A simple ground-peanut sauce base, echoing the flavor of daraba, used across many Chadian stews.
steps_detailed: Whisk the peanut butter slowly with 1 cup water, the tomatoes, and pepper, being generous with the pepper.
Simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.

description: A bold, peppery tomato sauce base, used across many Chadian stews, real versions genuinely fiery.
steps_detailed: Simmer everything together 12-15 minutes until thickened, being generous with both the chili powder and pepper.
